title: Fabrication of a microfluidic device for studying the combinatorial effect of physical and chemical cues on cell migration
protocol: Reconstitute Sylgard 527 by mixing equal mass of Part A and Part B provided by the manufacturer.
Prepare Sylgard 184 by mixing 10 parts base to one part curing agent, followed by vigorous mixing.
Degass the mixed Sylgard 184 for 20–30 minutes.
Mix above-prepared solutions of Sylgard 527 and Sylgard 184 in a ratio of 5:1 to obtain a stiffness of 30 kPa.
Mix above-prepared solutions of Sylgard 527 and Sylgard 184 in a ratio of 50:1 to obtain a stiffness of 3 kPa.
Coat the prepared PDMS mixture on a glass coverslip.
Bake the coated PDMS at 70°C for 10–12 hours.
Pour PDMS on a silicon master containing the desired design.
Incubate the wafer at 50°C–70°C in a hot air oven for 6–7 h.
Peel off the PDMS device from the master after incubation.
Spin coat the PDMS mixture (mix of Sylgard 527 and 184) on glass coverslips/slides using a spin coater at 600 rpm for 30 s to obtain a uniform surface coating of 150 μm.
Heat PDMS coated glass coverslips at 70°C in a hot air oven for 10–12 h to cure the coated PDMS.
Mix 10 parts of PDMS base with one part curing agent.
Degass the mixed PDMS to remove air bubbles.
Pour degassed PDMS onto a silicon wafer master.
Heat the PDMS-coated silicon wafer at 50°C–70°C for 6–7 hours in a hot air oven.
Peel off the cured PDMS from the silicon master after heating.
Cover peeled-off PDMS with scotch tape until further use to avoid dust deposition.
Clean fabricated devices using scotch tape to remove dust particles.
Punch inlets and outlets in the device using a 3 mm biopsy punch.
Optional: Autoclave microfluidic devices for long-duration cell culture purposes to prevent contamination.
Punch the prepared PDMS device at the inlet and outlet using a biopsy puncher.
Expose the punched device and prepared substrates to plasma for 1 minute.
Bond the exposed device and substrate together to form a complete device.
Check the devices and substrates under an inverted microscope prior to assembly.
Extracellular matrix (ECM) protein coating of the assembled microfluidic device.
Add ECM protein, such as collagen I at 50 μg/mL, through one inlet port.
Incubate the coated device for 10–12 hours at 4°C.
Wash the device with PBS two times before cell seeding.
Perfuse media through the inlet ports to remove unbound ECM protein.
Seed hMSCs from the cell seeding port on one side of the channel.
Allow cells to adhere for around 6 hours with continuous media replenishment every 1-2 hours.
Generate an EGF gradient in the device after cell attachment.
Capture images for 12 hours at 15-minute intervals using an inverted microscope equipped with an onstage incubator.
Culture human mesenchymal stem cells in a tissue culture flask with DMEM supplemented with 16% fetal bovine serum.
Take trypsinized single-cell suspension and count the number of cells.
Take 10 μL of resuspended suspension media containing ∼10,000 cells and introduce through one of the inlets.
Add 10 μL of complete media only from the other inlet and wait for 5 min to obtain pressure balance.
Incubate the device at 37°C.
Introduce EGF as a chemokine through opposite channel inlet (in the cell-free side) after cells have adhered to the substrate (∼6 h).
Perform time-lapse microscopy for 12 hours and capture images at a 15-minute interval.
Use manual cell tracker plugin of Image J (NIH) to quantify the cell motility.
